title: Product of Segments of Chords: 3D and Inner Product Generalization

problemStatement.formal: For a sphere in a real inner product space and an interior point P, prove that the product of chord segment lengths is r^2 - ||P-O||^2 and is independent of direction.
problemStatement.plain: Generalize the intersecting chords theorem from circles to spheres and arbitrary real inner product spaces.
whyMatters: Turns the chord intersection problem into a verified quadratic and Vieta calculation

proven: The chord intersection equation reduces to a monic quadratic in the line parameter.
The product of the two chord segment lengths is r^2 - ||P-O||^2 for interior points.
The result includes an explicit 3D sphere corollary and is fully verified for the OQ01 primary proof.
open: Extend the formalization to the external point/secant case.
Investigate analogous statements for complex inner product spaces.
knownResults.goal: Record the verified sphere and inner-product-space generalization of the chord product theorem.

currentState.focus: Verified source-backed record: primary proof has 228 lines, 5 public theorems plus 1 private helper theorem, 1 definition, 0 axioms, and 0 sorries.
currentState.nextAction: Optional follow-on: formalize the external secant case.

insights: The entire theorem depends only on inner-product-space algebra, not on the dimension of the ambient space.
The interior-point condition makes the two roots have opposite signs, converting the signed Vieta product into a product of distances.
The parent circle theorem is useful context but remains axiomatized separately; OQ01 itself has 0 axioms.
